lines.text: Jez Barton: Good afternoon everyone, and welcome to Transit.
Hello Sports Scientists!
My name is Jez Barton and today I’m going to talk to you about being a personal trainer.
Let me tell you a bit about myself.
After studying Sports Science at university, I worked on cruise ships for four years as a sports trainer.
Then I got married and wanted to stop travelling, so I got a job with a gym in Dubai.
For the last five years, I have had my own personal training business.
I’m sure you understand what personal training is, but I’ll start by giving you more information about the business.
Last year, the personal training industry was worth $9 billion in the USA, and £631 million in the UK.
Our industry is growing by 2.8% each year.
These days more people understand how important exercise is, so it’s not a luxury to have a personal trainer anymore.
There are about 300,000 personal trainers in the US and there will be another 30,000 over the next five years.
So, what does a personal trainer do and how much do we earn?
The average salary of a personal trainer in the US is $39,000 per year or around $18 an hour.
But if you work for yourself, you can charge much more.
In Dubai, the best trainers can earn $100,000 a year because there are lots of rich people in the city.
But this takes time.
You need to work on your own strengths and weaknesses first and develop your skills.
If you want to work with champion athletes, this isn’t a job for you.
Only a few of my customers play in sports teams, or compete in events.
Most of them are ordinary people.
My job is to support them and help them to achieve their personal fitness goals.
I get up early, usually at 4.30 am., since some of my clients come to me before work.
Sometimes I work for six hours with only a ten-minute break.
I don’t spend time with my children as much as I would like because I have customers who want to train after work, too.
But I love my job because it makes a difference to people’s lives.
Nearly 90% of personal trainers leave their jobs after the first year.
But those who stay, stay for the same reason.
It’s a great feeling when you see positive changes in a person’s life thanks to your personal training programme.

lines.text: Teacher: Today, you are going to present your research into scientists who have had an impact on astronomy and how we understand the stars and planets.
So we’ll begin with Yoko, who is going to talk about Isaac Newton, then Walid is going to tell us about Carl Sagan.
Yoko: Sir Isaac Newton was an English scientist who lived from 1643 to 1727.
He is one of the most remarkable scientists who ever lived.
Of course, he lived a long time before humans started exploring space, but he helped us to start to understand it better.
He invented a new kind of telescope – an object for looking at the stars – which meant people could see them more clearly.
Some of Newton’s work is not very easy to understand unless you are a mathematician.
His book, The Principles of Mathematics explained the movement of the planets around the sun.
It was an amazing achievement which changed people’s ideas about physics: at the time, we believed that the sun moved around the Earth.
Because Newton’s ideas were so new and different, they made some people very angry.
So it’s perhaps not surprising, that, later in life Newton stopped showing people his work.
Although everyone remembers Newton as a great scientist, he had some strange ideas, too.
Like many people at the time, Newton tried to change ordinary metal into gold and did lots of research about it.
Walid: Carl Sagan was an American astronomer who lived from 1934 to 1996.
His scientific achievements are not quite as amazing as Newton’s or Einstein’s.
However, Sagan knew how to explain complicated scientific ideas so that people could understand them.
He wrote popular books about astronomy and had a TV show called The Cosmos in the 1980s.
Because he was very excited about astronomy, he was able to show ordinary people how exciting it is, too – a talent that not many scientists have.
The show had 135 million viewers from all over the world, which, even today, is quite a few people.
However, some astronomers believed that Carl Sagan couldn’t be so popular and a serious scientist at the same time.
This was made worse when Sagan became one of the first scientists to talk about global warming.
At the time, no one understood his ideas very well and it became another reason why other scientists disliked him.

lines.text: Professor: Dr Ecker is here today to talk about how we can use drones to help with the problems created by global warming.
Dr Ecker: Yes, thank you for inviting me, Professor.
So, I think everybody here knows what a drone is.
It’s basically a flying computer – a bit like a small plane, controlled from the ground.
We can use drones in many different ways.
For example, we can send drones into different locations to collect information about the weather.
They help us to find out about how climates change over time – for example, how humid or dry they become.
Professor: And I believe you said that we can also use drones to plant trees?
Dr Ecker: Yes, as you know, we are cutting down trees in rainforests all over the world.
We’re trying to plant new trees at the same time, but the problem is that we cut down about 15 billion trees a year, but only plant 9 billion.
However, by using drones we can now plant trees from the air!
The drones fly three metres above the ground and are able to plant 120 trees per minute.
It’s actually possible to plant as many as 100,000 trees in one day.
Professor: That’s amazing!
Dr Ecker: In my opinion, one of the best ways that we use drones is for going into dangerous places, such as areas where there are forest fires or floods.
Drones can help us to find and save wildlife that is in danger.
Professor: So are there any disadvantages to drone technology?
For example, is it very expensive?
Dr Ecker: Well, drones are like computers.
You can get cheap ones, and you can get very expensive ones.
Our department at the university bought a drone last year for about 1,500 euros.
I tested more expensive ones and I personally feel that our drone is just as good.
It’s quite easy to use: we control it using an app from a mobile phone.
It can fly for 45 minutes at up to 40 kilometres per hour.
The problem with this kind of drone is that it uses batteries and obviously you have to charge them after flying, which can take up quite a lot of time.

lines.text: Jon: So Freyja, you are going to talk about an Icelandic festival.
Could you begin by telling us a bit about Iceland?
Freyja: Of course.
Well, Iceland is a small Northern European country in the Atlantic Ocean.
We have quite cold weather with snow and ice in winter, but the weather isn’t as cold as in Norway or Sweden.
Most of the country is still very rural and there are only a few big towns and one big city.

Because there are so many mountains and ice fields, there aren’t many places to build houses and towns, so about 80% of Icelanders live in or near the capital city of Reykjavik, on the south-west coast.
Jon: Tell us about Reykjavik.
Freyja: Well, it’s a very safe, clean city.
Since we have a good bus system and people like walking, there isn’t a lot of traffic or pollution.
The streets aren’t crowded, but that doesn’t mean it's boring!
Iceland has a long and ancient history so there are a lot of museums and other interesting places to visit in the city.
It’s the best place in the world to learn about the Vikings and other Northern European culture.
Many people come to Reykjavik for the festivals.
We have several music festivals, a design festival and, my favourite, the book festival.
Reading is a very popular activity in Iceland.
Perhaps it’s because of the long, dark winters when we have to stay inside a lot of the time.
People read a lot anyway, and we often give books as presents.
We have a lot of traditional literature and there are many new Icelandic books every year.
In fact, each year, more and more of them are translated into other languages.
Since everyone reads and writes so much, and the population is so small, it means that one in ten Icelanders will write a book in their lives!
Jon: Wow!
So is the festival just for books in the Icelandic language?
Freyja: No, writers from all over the world come to celebrate books and reading.
It’s a big international event.
The lectures, readings and workshops are in English and they are all free.
There are other sorts of entertainment, too, like dancing and parties.
It’s a great time to meet your favourite writers, taste traditional dishes and have fun.
Anyone who loves books should come.

lines.text: More and more people want to live in cities, but there are not enough houses and apartments.
Town planners need to solve this problem and create more places for people to live in crowded urban areas.
Today, we are going to look at one of these ways: building homes under the ground.
The idea of building places to live under the ground is not new.
In fact, some very ancient cities, like the cities of Derinkuyu and Kaymakli in Türkiye, were built more than 2,000 years ago in caves under the mountains of Anatolia.
People went into these cities to be safe in difficult times, and families lived in them with their animals for many months.
People also go under the ground to get away from the weather.
The Tunisian town of Matmata, in the Sahara Desert, was built in caves hundreds of years ago for this reason.
Below the ground was the best place to get away from the hot sun.
More recently, in Australia, the town of Coober Pedy was built in desert caves by people who came to work in the area.
As we know, the weather is very hot and dry, and the caves were the most comfortable place to live.
The first houses and apartments were built there in 1915, and about 3,000 people still live there today.
As the world gets more crowded, city buildings get taller.
But how far up can we go?
In some places, they have to stop building up into the sky, and the only way is down!
One interesting idea came from a company in Mexico – to build a whole city under the main square in Mexico City.
I think that will be a very difficult thing to do.
They want to put 55 floors of offices, apartments, businesses and shops under the city centre.
The 300-metre tower has a big window over the top to let in the light.
There are lots of plants on every tenth floor which help keep the air fresh and clean.
Also, I personally feel that people are happier if they can see plants and trees.
Another interesting idea comes from New York City where they are building the world’s first underground park.
It’s located in an old metro station, but it has grass and trees, just like any park.
Engineers want to test new technologies for getting air and light into spaces that are under the ground.
People hope that there will be enough sunlight to grow a forest!

lines.text: Professor: Today, Yu Yan and Liang are going to talk to us about traditional festivals in China.
And there are a lot of them – isn’t that right, Yu Yan?
Yu Yan: Yes.
Because Chinese culture is a very ancient culture, we have a long history and a lot of festivals.
Some are thousands of years old.
There are two types of festival – local ones, which people celebrate in certain areas of the country, and national festivals, which everyone celebrates.
We’re going to talk about the big national festivals and Liang’s going to begin with the Spring Festival.
Liang: Yes, the Spring Festival is the biggest holiday in China.
Everyone takes at least a week’s holiday from work and we all go home to our families.
The festival celebrates the Chinese New Year and it takes place at the end of January.
The traditional festival lasted a month.
Now, most people only celebrate Chinese New Year’s Day itself, and the day before it.
On the day before, we clean everything in our houses, and we decorate everything with the colour red – a lucky colour in China.
We prepare special dishes for the evening when people celebrate by eating a big dinner with their family and giving each other gifts.
Children get new clothes and gifts of money in red envelopes.
There are lots of fireworks to welcome the New Year.

On New Year’s Day, people go out in the streets to meet their friends and there are parades with traditional entertainment such as lion dancing with people dressed up in amazing traditional lion costumes.
Yu Yan: The next festival we are going to talk about is the Mid-autumn Festival.
This takes place near the beginning of October and it celebrates the moon.
It’s another festival when families usually get together.
The special dish for the festival is mooncakes which people give each other as gifts.
Making mooncakes is very important and every family has their own way to do it.
Families usually celebrate the Mid-autumn Festival with a big dinner.
One favourite activity is going outside to look at the moon.
Parents tell their children traditional stories about it.
In some parts of China parents try to find wives and husbands for their sons and daughters.

lines.text: Speaker: So, we’re going to look at some of the ways that technology has affected education and learning.
Nowadays, thanks to technology, information is available to everyone.
Most people have a PC, laptop or phone, so they only need to go online and they can find out information about almost anything.
It is easy to forget what a luxury this is and how much more difficult it was in the past.
Research took much longer because you had to be in the same location as your information.
People spent hours in libraries finding the right books and then looking through them.
Now, due to the internet, you don’t even need to get out of bed to research your essay!
But information is not the same as knowledge.
We can go online and see a lot of facts, but that does not mean we understand them.
And research shows that our memory can get worse due to computers – we become less able to remember details and facts.
Since the light from computer screens makes our eyes tired, we also pay less attention when we read online.
Research shows that many people understand a difficult new subject faster when they study it from books.
And children have problems, too.
For example, in primary schools many children’s handwriting is bad because they use a mouse and keyboard more than they hold a pencil.
Teenagers use technology and the internet for a large part of the day, which can affect their grades at school, their social lives and even their health.
Why should they go and meet friends in the park when they can just turn on their computers and chat with their friends from their bedrooms?
But technology has many more advantages than disadvantages, and it offers us many exciting new learning opportunities.
For example, there are lots of websites that teach you any skill you want, often for free.
You can learn languages, take dancing, cooking or art lessons, or watch videos explaining Einstein’s theory of relativity.
The most difficult thing is deciding where to start!

lines.text: Alex: The topic of today’s seminar is how climate change is affecting the Earth’s various climates.
At the beginning of the 19th century Wladimir Köppen, a German scientist, organized the world’s climates into five categories, which we still use today.
Global warming is affecting each of these climates in different ways.
Joss: Let’s begin with tropical climates, which are hot and humid with lots of rain.
A tropical climate has temperatures higher than 18°C all year.
Countries near the equator have tropical climates, including Brazil and Colombia in South America, the Congo in Africa and Malaysia and Indonesia in Asia.
As the weather gets hotter, they receive less rain.
This affects the rainforests.
There are more forest fires, which kill lots of wildlife.
People are also cutting down the rainforests, so many types of animals, plants and trees could disappear forever.
We need to look after the rainforests to save the plants and wildlife, and also because rainforests help to slow down global warming for the whole planet.
Alex: Next, the dry climate.
A dry climate is one in which there isn’t a lot of rain.
There are two types of desert climates: hot and cold.
Hot desert climates have hot temperatures all year round, for example Australia, most countries in the Middle East and North Africa.
On the other hand, cold desert climates have hot summers and cold winters, such as Argentina and Chile in South America, some countries in Central Asia.
In the future, the weather in these places will become even hotter and drier.
There will be droughts and people will need to use water very carefully.
Some areas, like Central Australia, could become so hot that people just won’t be able to live there anymore.
Joss: At the other extreme is the polar climate, the areas covering the North and South Pole.
The weather here is very cold, with temperatures never higher than 10°C.
The warmer global temperatures mean that the ice here is melting and sea levels are rising.
Scientists believe that Arctic and Antarctic wildlife are in danger due to the changing environment.
Alex: The final two categories we are going to talk about are the temperate climate, which has warm, humid summers and mild winters.
The continental climate has warm to cool summers and very cold winters.

lines.text: Host: Is it a good thing that football is such a big business these days?
I’m talking to club manager, Viktor Romanov, and player Obi Kanu who has just signed a contract with Westchester United.
Congratulations, Obi.
Obi: Thank you.
Host: Let’s start with Viktor.
Viktor, you’ve been a club manager for 30 years.
Do you think that there is too much money in football?
Viktor: Well, yes and no.
People are happy to spend lots of money on what they love.
In my opinion, if there’s a lot of money in football, it’s because of the fans.
And this is great because clubs can pay for players to have the best training, so they have more skills and get better and better.
Today’s players are the best ever.
Host: OK, so football players these days are very good, but the salaries they earn are still too much!
And the cost of tickets is too high.
Clubs charge so much money that many fans can’t afford to come to matches.
Viktor: OK, but fans can still watch the game on television.
A lot of money comes from television and advertising.
Clubs need that money very much.
The clubs often have money problems and the club managers worry about this more than anybody else.
We always have to make more money so we can attract champion players who will score goals and help us win matches.
Without those players, clubs cannot continue.
Host: So Obi, you trained at the famous Abidjan football academy in The Ivory Coast.
What’s your opinion of football as a business?
Obi: Well, The Ivory Coast is not a rich country.
I spent all my time as a kid kicking a football around with my friends in the street.
We all dreamed of getting into the academy.
It’s the one big chance to make money.
We had to compete with each other all the time.
The big prize is getting into a professional team; then you can support your family and give them a better life.
But you have to work hard and be strong.
You also have to be lucky to get the opportunity.
The football business is hardest of all for the players.
Clubs are businesses that buy and sell us.
If you get hurt and can’t play anymore, you can lose your job.
Nobody cares about you after that.

lines.text: Suzi: Hey Karl, Professor Garcia says another group has chosen our topic for their project.
We have to find a different one.
Karl: On no!
That was a great topic and we had good ideas about it … What can we look at instead?
Suzi: Well, how about the advantages and disadvantages for businesses of letting their employees work from home?
It’s a big thing at the moment and a lot of people are talking about it.
Karl: Mmm.
Do you think so?

I haven’t heard much about it. Will we be able to find enough to say about it? Suzi: Oh, yes! When you start to find out about it, the statistics are amazing! There are more and more people working from home. Last year, businesses saved $5 billion when people worked from home at least part of the time.
Karl: Wow!
That is amazing.
Why?
I don’t think I would want to work at home.
I like having colleagues and people to talk to.
Also, how do companies know that their employees are not taking long breaks and wasting time during the day instead of working?
Suzi: Well, they can ask employees to write down the hours they work.
And research shows that the productivity of people who work from home is 35–40% higher than those who stay in the office.
Karl: Really?
That surprises me.
Suzi: Well, think about it.
The employer sets the goals for what they want the employees to achieve, but the employees can choose how they spend their time during the day.
Eighty percent of home workers say their stress goes down.
They find time to exercise more, eat more healthily and feel better in general … And listen, one big US company says workers saved 17.4 million litres of petrol by working from home.
Karl: OK.
Maybe we’ve got a good idea here. What I’d like to find out is how much your personality helps you to be successful at home working.
I mean, you need good skills in how to manage your time, for example.
If your home is also where you work, your job could take over your whole life.
Suzi: Yes, you are right … But it says here that 60% of people who work from home say they have standard working hours 9 am to 5 pm, Monday to Friday.

lines.text: I have found the person – and the invention – I want to talk about for the inventions seminar.
His name is Alfredo Moser and he’s from Brazil.
Kym: At last!
Well, hurry up and tell us about him!
Tara: OK, well, Alfredo Moser invented the bottle lamp, which makes light out of old plastic bottles.
This is the best invention ever because the design is so simple, and it helps some of the poorest people in the world.
And it’s also a great achievement because it uses materials that we usually throw away and are a problem for the environment.
Vikram: That does sound quite interesting.
Tell us more.
Tara: The lamp is made by filling a plastic bottle with water and chlorine – you know, the chemical that we use in swimming pools – and then you put it in a sunny place.
It takes energy from the sun during the day and, at night, it lights up so you can use it as a lamp.
People who live in places with no electricity can use these bottle lamps.
They make it possible for children to do their homework in the evenings and families can spend time together.
It’s amazing!
Vikram: But surely it must be more complicated than that?
You can’t make a lamp out of a bottle of water!
Tara: Yes, you can.
Although you do need some sort of battery as well as the bottle and a few other simple things – they are cheap and easy to make.
Alfredo Moser’s life is remarkable in other ways, too.
The surprising thing about him is that he never tried to get rich from his invention.
He wasn’t interested in being an entrepreneur and starting a business.
His purpose was to help people.
The lamp was a big success all over the world, but he didn’t try to make money from it.
Kym: OK, that’s not a bad story.
Do you have any examples of situations in which the lamps are used?
Tara: Lots of places where many people are poor, and electricity is unusually expensive: in the Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Tanzania, Argentina, Fiji … all over the world, really.
People are even starting to grow food in small indoor farms, using light from the bottle lamps.

lines.text: Eli: I’ve just been reading about the reasons why space travel is difficult.
